input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date. Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 satisfies the preferred position in full: Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience on thirty days' written notice (no more than 30 days), Vendor must promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the post-termination period (pro rata) with no early-termination fee, and Vendor is expressly denied any corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term. No other provision confers a Vendor convenience right: Sections 9.1–9.3 are for-cause only, and Section 8.2 non-renewal is exercisable only by Customer. The take-or-pay language in Section 2.1 ("without reduction or termination rights") is in tension with Section 9.4's refund/no-penalty outcome, but that is the minimum-commitment bargain and is addressed under MINCOMMIT rather than flagged a second time here.
